claims.text: An integrated method combining phase-field modeling, dislocation dynamics, and customized interatomic potentials can concurrently optimize phase stability, microstructure refinement, and alloy properties.
The proposed method is applicable to a generic coarse-grained and/or multiphase metallic alloy.
Severe plastic deformation involves high pressures combined with significant shear at room or moderately elevated temperatures.
Simulation-derived parameters can guide severe-plastic-deformation processing.
The relevant severe-plastic-deformation conditions produce substantial shear and plastic strain without compromising material integrity.
A coupled phase-field/dislocation-dynamics framework models the evolution of phase interfaces and dislocation structures.
Customized interatomic potentials can represent structural properties, relative phase stability, chemical ordering, and deformation behavior in an alloy.
Integrating atomistic potentials with dislocation and phase-field models captures the energy landscape governing phase stability and microstructural evolution.
The integrated simulation framework facilitates a transition from a coarse microstructure to a refined microstructure during deformation.
The integrated simulation framework stabilizes desirable phases during severe plastic deformation.
Phase stabilization and microstructural refinement lead to an optimized balance of mechanical and physical properties.
Simulation-guided severe plastic deformation will produce enhanced phase stability and a uniformly refined microstructure.
Simulation-guided severe plastic deformation will improve mechanical and physical properties relative to conventional processing.
Conventional thermal and thermomechanical treatments are less effective at simultaneously controlling phase transformations and refining microstructure.
The predicted benefit is significant within deformation regimes typical of severe plastic deformation.
Processing beyond typical shear and pressure limits may cause material failures that are not represented by the simulation.
Scale-bridging approximations and complex interactions under severe deformation limit precise quantitative predictions of property enhancement.
